Required Public Postings

Public notices

All legally-required public postings for the Town of Millbrook are published on this page in addition to the printed posting board at Town Hall. Notices remain posted for the period required by statute or for at least seven calendar days, whichever is longer.

Active alerts (3)

Public Health Posted June 22, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. · Issued by Health Department

Boil-water advisory in effect — Harbor District (Zones 3 & 4)

A routine quarterly water sample taken at the Wharf Street sampling station on June 20 returned a turbidity level above the action threshold. As a precaution, the Town has issued a boil-water advisory for all residents and businesses served by water mains in Zones 3 and 4 (the Harbor District). Residents should bring tap water to a rolling boil for at least one minute, then let it cool, before using it for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, or making ice. The advisory will remain in effect until two consecutive clear samples are confirmed, expected within 48–72 hours.

Bottled water is available at no charge at the Harbor District Fire Station (47 Wharf Street) from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily. Limit: two cases per household. Residents who require home delivery should call the COA at (774) 555-0160.

Boil-water instructions (PDF) Affected addresses map Sign up for SMS updates
Weather Posted June 21, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. · Issued by Emergency Management

Heat advisory in effect through Wednesday, June 24

The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory through Wednesday evening with daytime heat-index values forecast at 96–102°F. Cooling centers are open at the Public Library (9–8 daily), Senior Center (8:30–7 extended hours), and Memorial Hall main room (10–6). Residents 70+ or with chronic conditions may request a wellness check by calling (774) 555-0160. Check on neighbors and never leave children or pets in a parked vehicle.

Cooling center hours & map Heat illness symptoms
Road Closure Posted June 19, 2026 · Issued by Department of Public Works

Mill Road bridge closure begins Monday, July 6 — approx. eight weeks

The Mill Road bridge over the Cobbett River will be closed to vehicular traffic beginning at 7:00 a.m. on Monday, July 6, 2026 for steel deck replacement. The closure is expected to last approximately eight weeks. Detour will route via Cobbett Bridge and Route 28A. The north pedestrian sidewalk will remain open throughout the project. Emergency vehicles will be diverted to the Cobbett Bridge route.

Detour map Construction schedule Contact project manager

Permit applications open for public comment

The following applications are open for written public comment. Submit comments to the listed reviewing body in writing or attend the corresponding public hearing.

Planning Board Comment deadline: June 23, 2026 · Application #SP-2026-007

Site plan review — 14 Wharf Street mixed-use redevelopment

Applicant proposes a four-story mixed-use building containing 1,800 sq. ft. of ground-floor retail, 22 residential units (including 4 affordable units), and a 28-space parking garage. Building height: 47 ft. Setback waivers requested from front and side property lines. The application is subject to design review under the Harbor District Form-Based Code.

Application narrative Site plan & renderings Traffic study Submit a comment
Zoning Board of Appeals Comment deadline: June 26, 2026 · Application #V-2026-018

Variance application — 88 Elm Street accessory dwelling unit

Property owner seeks dimensional variance from Section 4.3.2 of the Zoning Bylaw to permit construction of an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) within the existing rear-yard setback (proposed: 8 ft.; required: 15 ft.). The property is located within the R-2 residential district.

Variance application Site plan Submit a comment
Conservation Commission Comment deadline: June 24, 2026 · Notice of Intent #NOI-2026-022

Cobbett River bank stabilization — 88 Mill Road

Applicant proposes installation of approximately 240 linear feet of bio-engineered bank stabilization (live stake plantings with toe-of-slope stone) within the riverfront area. Work includes removal of three failing trees and replacement with native species. Filed under the Massachusetts Wetlands Protection Act and the local Wetlands Bylaw.

NOI form Stabilization plan Submit a comment
Historic District Commission Comment deadline: July 4, 2026 · Application #COA-2026-031

Certificate of Appropriateness — 4 Common Street window replacement

Applicant proposes replacement of original 6-over-6 wood sash windows with insulated wood-clad simulated divided light windows. Property is contributing structure within the Common Square Historic District (NRHP listed 1976). Comments solicited regarding compliance with the District’s Design Guidelines.
